title: Multiplication by $n$ is finite
statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety
over a field $k$, and let $n\geq1$. Then the map $[n]$ of
[def-sc-mult-n] is a finite homomorphism of
group schemes, and its kernel
$A[n]$ is a finite group scheme over $k$.

proof.text: The multiplication map [n] is a homomorphism of group schemes: A is commutative by [lem-sc-av-commutative], and the n-fold sum map is a homomorphism by [lem-sc-mult-n-homomorphism].

Let $K$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. The base change $A_K$ is a group scheme over $K$, proper and smooth since these properties are stable under base change, and connected because $A$ is connected with the $k$-rational point $e$, hence geometrically connected (Stacks Tag 04KV); so $A_K$ is an abelian variety over $K$ by [def-sc-abelian-variety], and $[n]_K$ is its multiplication by $n$. By [lem-sc-mult-n-locally-quasi-finite], $[n]_K$ is locally quasi-finite, so its fibres are finite. Since $A_K\to A$ is surjective and the fibre of $[n]_K$ over a point above $s\in A$ is the base change of the fibre $[n]^{-1}(s)$ along a field extension, every fibre of $[n]$ is finite; as $[n]$ is of finite type, it is locally quasi-finite, and it is quasi-compact because $A$ is proper over $k$, hence quasi-finite. By [def-sc-abelian-variety], $A$ is proper over $k$ and the target $A$ is separated, so $[n]$ is proper. Therefore [cor-pqf-proper-quasifinite-finite] gives that $[n]$ is finite.

source.place: proof, algebraically closed reduction and properness conclusion

proof.text: By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], A[n] is the fibre of [n] over the unit section. It is therefore the pullback of the finite morphism [n] along that section; finite morphisms are stable under pullback, so the pullback is finite. Hence A[n] is a finite group scheme.
